T1071.description: Adversaries may communicate using OSI application layer protocols to avoid detection/network filtering by blending in with existing traffic.
T1071.name: Application Layer Protocol

T1078.description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts as a means of gaining Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, or Defense Evasion.
T1078.name: Valid Accounts

T1078.004.description: Valid accounts in cloud environments may allow adversaries to perform actions to achieve Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, or Defense Evasion.
T1078.004.name: Cloud Accounts

T1087.description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of valid accounts, usernames, or email addresses on a system or within a compromised environment.
T1087.name: Account Discovery

T1110.description: Adversaries may use brute force techniques to gain access to accounts when passwords are unknown or when password hashes are obtained.
T1110.name: Brute Force

T1110.001.description: Adversaries with no prior knowledge of legitimate credentials within the system or environment may guess passwords to attempt access to accounts.
T1110.001.name: Password Guessing

T1110.003.description: Adversaries may use a single or small list of commonly used passwords against many different accounts to attempt to acquire valid account credentials.
T1110.003.name: Password Spraying

T1133.description: Adversaries may leverage external-facing remote services to initially access and/or persist within a network.
T1133.name: External Remote Services

T1566.description: Adversaries may send phishing messages to gain access to victim systems.
T1566.name: Phishing

T1566.001.description: Adversaries may send spearphishing emails with a malicious attachment in an attempt to gain access to victim systems.
T1566.001.name: Spearphishing Attachment

T1566.002.description: Adversaries may send spearphishing emails with a malicious link in an attempt to gain access to victim systems.
T1566.002.name: Spearphishing Link
